76-045.r: Kerala → India's largest thorium producer. Thorium comes from monazite; Indian Rare Earths Ltd processes it at Udyogamandal (Aluva), Ernakulam.

76-046.r: Kerala's coastal beaches → monazite, which also holds thorium and uranium; more than one option fits, so the book gives no single answer (*). Monazite is abundant in Kerala.

76-048.r: Monazite in India → Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, West Bengal, Maharashtra, Gujarat; both Tamil Nadu and Kerala fit, so no single answer (*).

76-049.r: Only 2 true: Kerala's monazite sands contain uranium (monazite: thorium, lanthanum, uranium, cerium). India has rich monazite deposits, so 'no thorium' is false.

76-050.r: Uranium centres: Domiasiat → Meghalaya; Lambapur → Andhra Pradesh (now Telangana); Rohil → Rajasthan; Gogi → Karnataka.

76-052.r: Turamdih (East Singhbhum, Jharkhand) → uranium, about 24 km from Jaduguda; mined by Uranium Corporation of India Ltd.

76-053.r: Chhattisgarh has all four: bauxite (Bastar, Bilaspur, Kabirdham, Surguja), dolomite (Bilaspur, Janjgir, Durg, Raipur), iron ore (haematite, Bastar), tin (Dantewada).

76-054.r: Palamu → bauxite; Hazaribagh → mica; Khetri → copper; Keonjhar → manganese. No printed code matches, so the book gives no single answer (*).

76-055.r: Chhota Nagpur plateau → rich in many minerals (its main resource).

76-056.r: Kaimur plateau (Rohtas and Kaimur districts, Bihar) → limestone and sandstone; Banjari cement industry uses its limestone.

76-057.r: Coal → Giridih (Jharkhand); Copper → Alwar (Rajasthan); Manganese → Dharwar (Karnataka); Lignite → Jayamkondam (Tamil Nadu).

76-058.r: Gurumahisani → iron ore; Talcher → coal; Jaduguda → uranium; Zawar → lead.

76-059.r: Only Nickel–Odisha right (~93% of resources). Copper → Rajasthan (~52.25%), tungsten → Karnataka (~41.0%), not Jharkhand or Kerala (IMYB 2024).

76-060.r: Guru Mahisani → iron ore; Talcher → coal; Jaduguda → uranium; Zawar → zinc.

76-061.r: Salt 2022-23: India 3rd in world (after China, USA), ~280 lakh t; sea salt ~82%; Gujarat 87%, Rajasthan 6%, Tamil Nadu 4.7%. Book gives no single answer (*).

76-062.r: Correct pair: Bauxite–Lohardaga (Jharkhand). Koderma → mica, Talcher → coal, Bailadila → iron ore.

76-063.r: Main uses: Limestone → cement; Copper → electrical goods; Bauxite → aeroplane manufacturing; Manganese → steel.

76-064.r: India's first lithium mine → Katghora, Korba district, Chhattisgarh (announced August 2024); lithium 10–2,000 ppm over about 250 hectares.

77-001.r: NTPC Singrauli → NTPC's first unit (set up 1977), in Sonbhadra (UP), not Chhattisgarh. Singrauli region: Sidhi (MP) + Sonbhadra (UP); Rihand in Sonbhadra; Vindhyachal in Singrauli district (MP).

77-002.r: Idukki (Periyar river, Kerala) → hydroelectric, not thermal. Correct: Sabarigiri → hydro (Kerala); Ghatprabha → irrigation; Ramganga → multipurpose → 2, 3 and 4.

77-003.r: Thermal plants: Ukai → Gujarat; Patratu → Jharkhand; Pench → Madhya Pradesh; Dabhol → Maharashtra.

77-004.r: Uran gas turbine power station (gas-based) → Raigad district, Maharashtra.

77-005.r: Coal → India's largest energy source; thermal power has the highest share. Installed capacity 31 December 2025: 513729.69 MW; thermal 48.07% (coal 219610.00 MW).

77-007.r: Installed capacity, 31 December 2025: Thermal 246941.62 MW > Wind 54510.93 > Hydro 50914.66 > Nuclear 8780 → matches no option; the book gives no single answer (*).

77-008.r: Installed capacity order (when asked): water (hydro) > natural gas > nuclear > diesel → 1, 2, 3, 4.
77-008.c: The book calls 54510.93 MW India's total installed capacity (31 December 2025), but that is its figure for wind power; the all-India total is far larger.

77-009.r: NTPC super thermal plant in West Bengal → Farakka (at Nabarun, Murshidabad district); coal-based.

77-010.r: Map question: '2' = Srisailam (hydroelectric, Telangana), not thermal. Thermal: 1 Ukai (Gujarat), 3 Korba (Chhattisgarh), 4 Obra (Uttar Pradesh).

77-011.r: Coal power plants: Kahalgaon → Bihar; Khargone → Madhya Pradesh; Korba → Chhattisgarh; Kudgi → Karnataka.

77-012.r: Neyveli thermal plant (Tamil Nadu) → fed by lignite, a Tertiary coal; first lignite-fired power station in South-East Asia.

77-013.r: Ramagundam Super Thermal Power Station → then Andhra Pradesh (now Telangana); capacity 2600 MW.

77-014.r: Obra Thermal Power Station (Sonbhadra, UP) → built with Russian help, 1967.

77-015.r: Kothagudem → Andhra Pradesh (now Telangana); Raichur → Karnataka; Mettur → Tamil Nadu; Wanakbori → Gujarat.

77-016.r: Wrong pair: Paras–Andhra Pradesh; Paras is in Maharashtra. Correct: Badarpur–Delhi, Harduaganj–Uttar Pradesh, Utran–Gujarat.

77-017.r: Installed thermal capacity (31.12.2025): Maharashtra 27839.02 MW > Uttar Pradesh 26580.42 > Gujarat 24174.89 > West Bengal 8514.34. No code fits (*).

77-018.r: Thermal PLF was 70–75% when asked. Recent all-India PLF (coal & lignite): 2021-22 58.87%, 2023-24 69.09%, 2024-25 69.45%, 2025-26 (P) 65.54%.
